# Sparse versus partial index equivalence — facts

> Source-anchored units about Sparse versus partial index equivalence: 15 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 15 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] For a compound sparse index containing only ascending/descending keys, a document is indexed when at least one indexed field exists. Consequently, replacing sparse {a:1,b:1} with a partial filter requiring only b, or requiring both a and b, changes membership. Matching the documented inclusion rule requires an OR of the two existence tests; this is a logical derivation, not a guarantee of identical plans. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md
- [statement] A partial index is eligible only when the query establishes its filter or a stricter subset; merely having a useful key pattern is insufficient. Percona demonstrates a false-only partial index being used for flag:false while flag:true takes a collection scan. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/using-partial-and-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb/
- [statement] SERVER-28889 records the redundant-filter FETCH improvement as fixed in 7.0.0-rc5 and 7.1.0-rc0. Its linked existence-predicate issue SERVER-26896 is separate, so that fix alone does not prove all existence-filter coverage cases are solved. This is the issue record updated 2026-09-21, not a claim about every later release. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-28889 · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] For normal planner selection, a query must imply the partial filter, either by including it or a more restrictive condition. A query on an indexed field alone cannot generally use an index filtered on another field if matching documents outside the filter would be lost. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/
- [statement] A sparse index normally cannot supply queries that need omitted documents. Forcing it with hint can return incomplete results, including an incorrect whole-collection count. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/mongodb-index-type-and-properties-series-2
- [statement] Partial filters can reference non-key fields and restrict values, so partial indexes support subsets that sparse:true cannot express. Mydbops illustrates an index on name filtered by existence of email. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/mongodb-index-type-and-properties-series-2
- [statement] Historical evidence disproves blanket execution-plan interchangeability: SERVER-29247 reports extra FETCH work for partial-index counts in MongoDB 3.4.4; an independent Stack Overflow reproduction reports document fetches with partial filters in 4.2.1, 4.2.7 and 4.4.0-rc9. These reports establish historical behavior, not a current-version limitation. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-29247 · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62342543/covered-queries-do-not-work-with-partial-indices

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A MongoDB 2.6.5 user reported E11000 for a unique sparse {userId:1,name:1} index when repeated userId values paired with null name values. This is a historical first-hand failure example of mistaking compound sparsity for optional non-null uniqueness, rather than evidence of a current server defect. (low confidence) — https://stackoverflow.com/questions/26711235/mongodb-can-not-create-unique-sparse-index-duplicate-key · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence
- [statement] An index definition cannot combine sparse and partialFilterExpression; a migration must create the desired alternative definition rather than turn on both options. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.mydbops.com/blog/mongodb-index-type-and-properties-series-2

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For a single ascending or descending field x, {x:1} with sparse:true has the same document-inclusion behavior as the same key with partialFilterExpression:{x:{$exists:true}}; MongoDB documents the partial form as supporting the same queries as the sparse form. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/using-partial-and-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb/
- [statement] Existence is different from non-nullness: sparse indexes retain explicit null values and skip missing fields. The equivalent $exists:true partial filter also retains null; neither form means index only non-null values. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/partial-index-equivalent-to-sparse/219177, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md
- [statement] Partial indexes can filter on non-key fields and value conditions; for example, an index on city and surname can include only documents with age below 30. This is more expressive than the sparse presence rule. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-index-usage-and-mongodb-explain-part-1/, https://www.percona.com/blog/using-partial-and-sparse-indexes-in-mongodb/
- [statement] A sparse unique index permits multiple documents omitting the indexed field but still indexes explicit null. With a partial unique index, uniqueness applies only to documents satisfying its filter; changing that filter changes the population subject to uniqueness. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md
- [statement] Historical partial-index coverage limitations should be version-scoped: SERVER-28889 recorded an unnecessary FETCH for a predicate already guaranteed by a partial filter and lists fixes in 7.0.0-rc5 and 7.1.0-rc0. SERVER-26896 separately tracks covering $exists predicates. Equal index membership alone is insufficient evidence of an identical covered plan; inspect explain on the target server. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-28889 · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-26896, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62342543/covered-queries-do-not-work-with-partial-indices
- [statement] The any-key rule does not extend unchanged to compound indexes containing geospatial or text keys; their documented sparse membership depends on the special-type fields. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: Sparse versus partial index equivalence
